messages.subject: Minimal plotmath example on github/wiki fails.
parts:
Dear all,

I would like to have greek letters as legend key labels. I found the
link
https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/wiki/Plotmath (suggested by
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/5293715/how-to-use-greek-symbols-in-ggplot2
)
but the minimal example (see the code below) given there does not
work. I obtain:
Error in data.frame(alpha == 3.1415, beta == 3.1415, check.names =
FALSE, : object 'alpha' not found
Does anyone know how to fix this?

Cheers,

Marius

PS:
> sessionInfo()

library(ggplot2)

d <- data.frame(x=1:10,y=1:10,f=rep(c("alpha","beta"),each=5),
stringsAsFactors=FALSE)

value <- 3.1415
my.labs <- list(bquote(alpha==.(value)),bquote(beta==.(value)))

qplot(x,y,data=d,colour=f) +
scale_colour_manual(values=1:2,breaks=c("alpha","beta"),
labels=my.labs)

parts:
Okay, after using devtools, I could manage to run the code from the minimal example. However, it did not work for my original example code (see below; I obtain "Error: Continuous value supplied to discrete scale"):

### minimal example:

## install the following:
## install_github("scales")
## install_github("ggplot2", "hadley", "develop")
## install_github("ggplot2", "kohske", "feature/new-guides-with-gtable")

## now run:
require(devtools)
dev_mode(TRUE)
require(ggplot2)

d <- data.frame(x=1:10, y=1:10, f=rep(c("alpha","beta"),each=5), stringsAsFactors=FALSE)

value <- 3.1415
my.labs <- list(bquote(alpha==.(value)), bquote(beta==.(value)))

qplot(x,y,data=d,colour=f) +
scale_colour_manual(values=1:2, breaks=c("alpha","beta"), labels=my.labs)
## => works

### now the same logic applied to a slightly more complicated example:
require(devtools)
dev_mode(TRUE)
require(ggplot2)
require(reshape2)

## parameters of some model
p1 <- c(20, 50, 100, 200)
p2 <- c(5, 10, 20, 50, 100)
p3 <- c("group.1","group.2","group.3","group.4","group.5")
p4 <- c(0.2, 0.5, 0.8)

## replications
N <- 1000

## lengths
l1 <- length(p1)
l2 <- length(p2)
l3 <- length(p3)
l4 <- length(p4)

## build result array containing the measurements
arr <- array(rep(NA, l1*l2*l3*l4*N), dim=c(l1, l2, l3, l4, N),
dimnames=list(
p1=p1,
p2=p2,
p3=p3,
p4=p4,
N=1:N))

## fill the result array (dummy here) with values
for(i in 1:l1){
for(j in 1:l2){
for(k in 1:l3){
for(l in 1:l4){
arr[i,j,k,l,] <- i+j+k+l+runif(N)
}
}
}
}

## create molten data
mdf <- melt(arr, formula = . ~ + p1 + p2 + p3 + p4 + N) # create molten data frame
colnames(mdf) # => fine
stopifnot(dim(mdf)==c(l1*l2*l3*l4*N, 6))

## build means (dummy function here)
mdf.mean <- dcast(mdf, p1 + p2 + p3 + p4 ~ "Value", fun.aggregate=mean, value_var="value")
str(mdf.mean)

## add p1 legend labels
my.labs <- lapply(1:4, function(l) bquote(alpha==.(l)))

## plot
ggplot(mdf.mean, aes(x=p2, y=Value, colour=p1)) + geom_point() +
geom_line(aes(group=p1)) + facet_grid(p3 ~ p4, space="free") +
scale_x_continuous(limits=c(1,max(p2)), breaks=p2, labels=p2) +
scale_colour_manual(values=1:length(p1), breaks=unique(mdf.mean$p1),
labels=my.labs)
## => why do I receive "Error: Continuous value supplied to discrete scale"?

Cheers,

Marius


require(devtools)
dev_mode(TRUE)
require(ggplot2)
require(reshape2)

## parameters of some model
p1 <- c(20, 50, 100, 200)
p2 <- c(5, 10, 20, 50, 100)

p4 <- c(0.2, 0.5, 0.8)

l3 <- length(p3)
l4 <- length(p4)

## build result array containing the measurements

dimnames=list(
p1=p1,
p2=p2,
p3=p3,
p4=p4,
N=1:N))

## fill the result array (dummy here) with values
for(i in 1:l1){
for(j in 1:l2){
for(k in 1:l3){
for(l in 1:l4){
arr[i,j,k,l,] <- i+j+k+l+runif(N)
}
}
}
}

## create molten data
mdf <- melt(arr, formula = . ~ + p1 + p2 + p3 + p4 + N) # create molten data frame
colnames(mdf) # => fine
stopifnot(dim(mdf)==c(l1*l2*l3*l4*N, 6))

## build means (dummy function here)
mdf.mean <- dcast(mdf, p1 + p2 + p3 + p4 ~ "Value", fun.aggregate=mean, value_var="value")
str(mdf.mean)

## add p1 legend labels
my.labs <- lapply(1:4, function(l) bquote(alpha==.(l)))

## plot
mdf.mean. <- mdf.mean
mdf.mean.$p1 <- as.factor(mdf.mean.$p1)
ggplot(mdf.mean., aes(x=p2, y=Value, colour=p1)) + geom_point() +

geom_line(aes(group=p1)) + facet_grid(p3 ~ p4, space="free") +
scale_x_continuous(limits=c(1,max(p2)), breaks=p2, labels=p2) +

scale_colour_manual(name="", values=1:length(p1), breaks=unique(mdf.mean$p1),
labels=my.labs)

mdf.mean <- within(mdf.mean, {
P1 <- factor(p1, levels = c(20, 50, 100, 200))

scale_x_continuous(limits=c(1,max(p2)), breaks=p2, labels=p2) +
